title: PWA shell
lead: Add a manifest, icons and a minimal service worker so larder can be installed on Android (ADR 0004).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** offline editing or sync; push notifications.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A non-technical household member reaches larder through a home-screen icon. Since Chrome 108 on Android, installing from the menu doesn't need a fetch handler, but the install prompt does (docs/research/https-lan.md).

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
1. App icon: resolved by S52 (Brand mark and app icons); copy the 192, 512 and maskable 512 exports from the branding repo.
2. Theme and background colors? (S52 uses the brand background `#0f1419` and teal `#6ee7d2`.)
3. Display mode: `standalone` (recommended)?
4. Start URL: the Today view (recommended).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write a manifest with name, short_name, icons, start_url, display and colors.
2. Service worker: cache static assets only; network-first for pages; include a fetch handler.
3. Register the service worker in the base template.
4. Add a route serving `sw.js` at `/sw.js` for root scope.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- PWA tests pass.
- Chrome desktop DevTools → Application → Manifest shows no installability errors when served over HTTPS or localhost.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
